mainTopic: שמואל's view on extinguishing coals, burning impure libations, and which חטאות require laundering of blood-splashed garments
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge about שמואל. He allows putting out a metal coal on שבת but not a wood coal, so how can he follow רבי שמעון? The גמרא answers that he follows רבי שמעון on דבר שאין מתכוין, but follows רבי יהודה on מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. Next, רב הונא rules that impure libations are burned on their own woodpile inside the Temple, based on 'בקדש באש תשרף'. A ברייתא supports him, and שמואל wanted to announce this ruling in front of ten people. Then פרק כל התדיר ends, and a new משנה teaches that blood of any valid חטאת, eaten or inner, that splashes on a garment requires כיבוס, while blood of a disqualified חטאת does not. The גמרא asks why a bird חטאת is left out. It works through the words of the פסוק: 'תשחט' (shall be slaughtered), ״תורת״ (the law of), which includes, and ״זאת״ (this), which excludes. The amud ends as the גמרא begins explaining why the inner animal חטאות are the ones included, since they are more like the eaten חטאות. That list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why can't a wood coal be put out too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that שמואל follows רבי שמעון. שמואל forbids putting out a wood coal, but רבי שמעון's view would seem to allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל ruled you may put out a metal coal, but not a wood coal. If you think he holds like רבי שמעון, then even a wood coal should be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of שמואל's ruling: you may put out a metal coal, but not a wood coal. It then asks how this fits with the idea that שמואל follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a labor done without needing its normal purpose (מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה) is not forbidden by Torah law. Putting out a wood coal so that people won't get hurt is exactly that kind of labor. So if שמואל followed רבי שמעון, a wood coal should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: a burning coal
a wood coal, where putting it out can be a Torah-level labor
and if it enters your mind (introduces a challenge to an assumption)
he holds, he is of the opinion

phrases.english: but not a coal of wood.
And if it enters your mind
that he holds like Rabbi Shimon,
then even a wood coal too [should be allowed]!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf, which explained שמואל's view as following רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that שמואל follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון would allow putting out a wood coal, since it is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. Yet שמואל forbids it.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי שמעון on one rule and רבי יהודה on another
steps.stepSummary: שמואל follows רבי שמעון on unintended acts. On a labor done without needing its normal purpose, he follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On an act you don't intend, he holds like רבי שמעון. On a labor not needed for its own purpose, he holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון actually has two separate rules. שמואל accepts only one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דבר שאין מתכוין means the forbidden result happens without your intending it. On this, שמואל agrees with רבי שמעון that it is allowed. On מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, he holds like רבי יהודה that it is forbidden by Torah law, so a wood coal may not be put out.

keyTerms.meaning: an act whose forbidden result you did not intend
a labor done without needing its normal purpose
he holds it (follows that view)

steps.whatToRemember: These are two different rules. Someone can follow רבי שמעון on דבר שאין מתכוין and still follow רבי יהודה on מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two terms. דבר שאין מתכוין is about not intending the result at all. מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה is about doing the act on purpose, just not for its usual goal.

phrases.english: Regarding an unintended act,
he holds like Rabbi Shimon;
regarding a labor not needed for its own purpose,
he holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the opinion: שמואל follows רבי שמעון on one rule but not the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי שמעון means accepting all of his leniencies.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי שמעון only on דבר שאין מתכוין. On מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה he follows רבי יהודה, so a wood coal stays forbidden.

steps.title: Impure libations are burned on their own woodpile
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that wine libations that became impure are burned on a separate woodpile inside the Temple, based on 'בקדש באש תשרף'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Libations that became impure, one makes a separate woodpile for them and burns them, because it says 'in the holy place it shall be burned with fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא teaches how to get rid of wine libations that became impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impure libations are not taken out of the Temple. They are burned there on their own fire. The source is the פסוק requiring disqualified offerings to be burned 'בקדש', in the holy place.

keyTerms.meaning: wine libations poured on the altar
that became ritually impure
an arranged pile of wood for burning
by themselves, separately

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Libations that became impure,
one makes a woodpile for them
by themselves and burns them,
because it is stated:
"In the holy place it shall be burned with fire."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the coal discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure libations are burned on their own woodpile inside the Temple, as the פסוק 'בקדש באש תשרף' requires.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule and applies it to impure blood, oil, meal offerings and libations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught so: The blood, the oil, the meal offerings and the libations that became impure, one makes a separate woodpile for them and burns them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms רב הונא's ruling. It also shows the rule is wider: impure blood, oil and meal offerings are treated the same way as libations.

keyTerms.meaning: it is also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)
meal offerings
oil used with offerings

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
The blood and the oil
and the meal offerings and the libations that became impure,
one makes a woodpile for them
by themselves and burns them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא's ruling from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that impure libations are burned separately
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing blood, oil, meal offerings and libations

steps.title: שמואל wants to announce the ruling publicly
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asks רב חנא בגדתאה to gather ten people so he can announce the same ruling about impure libations in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב חנא בגדתאה: Bring me a group of ten, and I will tell you in front of them: Libations that became impure, one makes a separate woodpile for them and burns them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how שמואל wanted to teach this same rule publicly, in front of ten people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל teaches the same ruling as רב הונא and the ברייתא. Asking for ten people shows he wanted this הלכה to be widely known.

keyTerms.meaning: a group of ten people
in front of them
bring me

steps.whatToRemember: Impure libations, along with impure blood, oil and meal offerings, are burned on their own woodpile inside the Temple. רב הונא, a ברייתא and שמואל all agree on this.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to
Rav Chana of Baghdad:
Bring me a group of ten,
and I will tell you in front of them:
Libations that became impure,
one makes a woodpile for them
by themselves and burns them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds שמואל as another authority holding the same ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל, in front of ten people, states that impure libations are burned on their own woodpile.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל התדיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally finishes the chapter called כל התדיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'כל התדיר'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional closing line that marks the end of פרק כל התדיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every chapter of the גמרא ends with הדרן עלך, which means 'we will return to you,' followed by the chapter's name. It tells you the סוגיא about libations and the earlier topics is finished. A new chapter with a new topic starts right after.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the closing formula said at the end of a chapter
The name of the chapter now ending, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter 'Kol HaTadir'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter in which steps 1-5 appeared.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק כל התדיר is complete. A new chapter begins.

steps.title: Blood of every kind of sin offering on a garment must be laundered
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that blood of a חטאת that splashed on a garment requires כיבוס. This applies both to eaten חטאות and to inner חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blood of a חטאת splashed onto a garment, the garment must be laundered. The פסוק is talking about חטאות that are eaten, since it says 'in a holy place it shall be eaten.' Even so, both eaten חטאות and inner חטאות require laundering, because the פסוק says 'the law of the חטאת', meaning one law for all חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The new chapter opens with a משנה that sets a rule: a garment splashed with blood of a חטאת must be laundered. The rule covers inner חטאות too, not only the ones that are eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about כיבוס appear in the section about a חטאת that is eaten, so you might limit the rule to that kind. The משנה says no. The opening words 'תורת החטאת' make it one law for every חטאת, so the inner חטאות, whose blood goes inside, are included too.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of a sin offering
That splashed or sprayed
Laundering the garment
חטאות whose meat is eaten; their blood goes on the outer מזבח
Inner חטאות whose blood is brought inside; they are burned, not eaten
One law that applies to all of them

steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase 'one law for all חטאות' is the exact phrase the גמרא will use to build its challenge in step 9.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ דַּם חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּתַּז עַל הַבֶּגֶד –
phrases.english: MISHNA: Blood of a sin offering that sprayed onto a garment –
that garment requires laundering,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
phrases.english: even though the verse is speaking
only about the eaten ones –
phrases.notes: He means sin offerings whose meat gets eaten. The laundering פסוק is ויקרא ו:כ.

phrases.english: as it says: 'In a holy place it shall be eaten.'
Both the eaten ones and the inner ones
require laundering,
as it says: 'the law of the sin offering' –
one law for all the sin offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ דַּם חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּתַּז עַל הַבֶּגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of any valid חטאת, whether eaten or inner, that splashes on a garment requires כיבוס, because of 'תורת החטאת', one law for all חטאות.

steps.title: Blood of a disqualified sin offering does not require laundering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: a disqualified חטאת does not cause כיבוס. It then gives examples of a חטאת that was once fit and of one that was never fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A disqualified חטאת: its blood does not require laundering. This is true whether it once had a time when it was fit or never had one. Which one had a time of fitness? One left overnight, one that became impure, and one taken outside. Which one never had a time of fitness? One slaughtered with intent for outside its time or outside its place, and one whose blood was received by disqualified people.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit to the rule. The blood of a disqualified חטאת never requires כיבוס. Then it gives examples of the two kinds of disqualified חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a חטאת that was once fit and only later became disqualified still has 'real' blood that needs laundering. The משנה rejects this: once disqualified, no כיבוס is needed in either case. A חטאת left overnight, made impure, or taken out was fit at first. Wrong intent at slaughter or improper people receiving the blood make it unfit from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: A disqualified sin offering
A period of time when it was fit
That was left overnight
With intent for beyond its proper time
People who are unfit to do Temple service

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of כיבוס applies only to the blood of a valid חטאת, eaten or inner. Blood of a disqualified חטאת never requires it, whether it was once fit or never fit.

phrases.aramaic: חַטָּאת פְּסוּלָה – אֵין דָּמָהּ טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס,
phrases.english: A disqualified sin offering – its blood does not require laundering,
whether it had a period of fitness

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: or it did not have a period of fitness.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזוֹ הִיא שֶׁהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר?
phrases.english: Which is one that had a period of fitness?
One left overnight, one that became impure, and one that went out.
phrases.notes: 'Went out' means it was taken outside the Temple courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר?
phrases.english: And which is one that did not have a period of fitness?
One slaughtered for beyond its time or outside its place,
and one whose blood disqualified people received (and sprinkled).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, 'and sprinkled'.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטָּאת פְּסוּלָה אֵין דָּמָהּ טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from step 7 so that it applies only to a valid חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of a disqualified חטאת does not require כיבוס, whether it once had a period of fitness or never had one.

steps.title: If all sin offerings share one law, why is a bird sin offering excluded?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה. 'One law for all חטאות' should include a חטאת העוף, yet a ברייתא learns from the word 'זאת' that a חטאת העוף does not require כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Blood of a חטאת that splashed...' Now, if there is one law for all חטאות, even a bird חטאת should be included too! Why then does a ברייתא teach: 'You might think the blood of a bird חטאת requires laundering. That is why the פסוק says "זאת" (this).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה and then attacks it. The משנה's broad phrase 'one law for all חטאות' seems to clash with a ברייתא that leaves out the bird חטאת. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used 'תורת החטאת' to include every kind of חטאת. A חטאת העוף is also a חטאת, so it should be included too. But the ברייתא uses the word 'זאת' to limit the rule and exclude the bird. The גמרא needs to explain what makes the bird different from the inner חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird sin offering
'Why then was it taught?': introduces a source that seems to contradict
'You might think': introduces an idea the ברייתא is about to reject
'The פסוק teaches': introduces the word in the פסוק that gives the answer
'This': a limiting word in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. Both the משנה and the ברייתא are accepted. The question is only how they fit together, and the answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'Blood of a sin offering (that died) [that sprayed]' etc.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording, 'that sprayed', which matches the משנה.

phrases.english: And if there is one law for all sin offerings,
then even a bird sin offering too!
Why then was it taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל תְּהֵא דַּם חַטַּאת הָעוֹף טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס?
phrases.english: You might think the blood of a bird sin offering requires laundering?
The verse says: 'This.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ו:יח, 'זאת תורת החטאת', 'This is the law of the sin offering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי תּוֹרָה אַחַת לְכׇל חַטָּאוֹת אֲפִילּוּ חַטַּאת הָעוֹף נָמֵי אַלְּמָה תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's derivation in step 7 and challenges how broad it is.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's derivation 'תורת החטאת: one law for all חטאות'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the phrase includes every חטאת, it should include a חטאת העוף. Yet a ברייתא learns from 'זאת' that a חטאת העוף does not require כיבוס, which seems to contradict the משנה's broad rule.

steps.title: The word 'shall be slaughtered' limits the law to slaughtered offerings
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting בר קפרא, explains that the פסוק says ״תִּשָּׁחֵט״, so it is talking only about offerings that are slaughtered. That leaves out a חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of בר קפרא: The verse says 'shall be slaughtered.' This means the verse is speaking about offerings that are slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9: why the משנה's 'all חטאות' does not include a bird. The answer is that the פסוק itself is limited to slaughtered animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about כיבוס sits right next to the words 'where the עולה is slaughtered, the חטאת shall be slaughtered.' Since the topic is slaughtered offerings, a bird is outside the topic, because it is not slaughtered. So the משנה's 'all חטאות' means all slaughtered חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall be slaughtered,' a word in the פסוק
Offerings that are slaughtered with a knife

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Bar Kappara:
The verse says: 'shall be slaughtered.'
The verse is speaking about offerings that are slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the פסוק by a word in it
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is only about slaughtered offerings, so the bird is not part of 'all חטאות'

steps.title: Maybe the verse only covers sin offerings that are eaten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another way to limit the פסוק: maybe it covers only eaten חטאות, because the פסוק says 'in a holy place it shall be eaten.' Then the inner חטאות would be left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead that the verse is speaking about offerings that are eaten, as it is written: 'In a holy place it shall be eaten.' Then the inner sin offerings would not be included!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that inner חטאות also need כיבוס. It points to another word in the same passage that might limit the law even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we limit the פסוק by the word 'slaughtered,' why not also limit it by the word 'eaten'? The inner חטאות are slaughtered but not eaten. So this reading would leave them out, which goes against the משנה in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say instead,' an alternative reading suggested as a challenge
Offerings that are eaten by the כהנים
Inner חטאות, whose blood is brought inside the היכל; they are burned, not eaten

phrases.english: But say that the verse is speaking about offerings that are eaten,
as it is written: 'In a holy place it shall be eaten.'
But inner sin offerings would not be included!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the limiting method of step 10 to challenge the inclusion of inner חטאות
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling (step 7) that inner חטאות cause כיבוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one word in the passage ('slaughtered') can limit the law, another word in the passage ('eaten') should limit it too, and that would leave out the inner חטאות

steps.title: The word 'law of' includes the inner sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: The תורה wrote ״תּוֹרַת הַחַטָּאת״, 'the law of the חטאת.' That wording includes all slaughtered חטאות, even the inner ones that are not eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One included more by writing 'the law of.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The phrase 'the law of the חטאת' is a broad phrase that brings the inner חטאות back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״תּוֹרַת״ means one law for the whole group. That cancels the limit from the word 'eaten,' so the inner חטאות, which are slaughtered but not eaten, are included. The next step asks whether this broad word should then bring in the bird as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Included more; a word that widens the law
'The Merciful One,' meaning the תורה
'The law of,' an inclusive word in the פסוק

phrases.english: The Merciful One included more by writing 'the law of.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק opens with 'זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַחַטָּאת', 'this is the law of the חטאת' (ויקרא 6:18).

steps.terutzResolutionType: An inclusive word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'The law of' includes the inner חטאות as well

steps.title: Then the bird sin offering should be included too
steps.stepSummary: If ״תּוֹרַת״ widens the law, it should also bring in a חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even a bird sin offering should be included too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If 'the law of' can include the inner חטאות, why can't it also include a bird?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״תּוֹרַת״ was strong enough to override the limit from 'eaten.' So why should it not override the limit from 'slaughtered' as well? Then the bird would come back in.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so,' introducing a problem that follows from the last answer
'Also, too'

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ חַטַּאת הָעוֹף נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, then even a bird sin offering should be included too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ חַטַּאת הָעוֹף נָמֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ״תּוֹרַת״ to include more
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inclusive word should include every kind of חטאת, the bird among them

steps.title: The word 'this' leaves out the bird sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The word ״זֹאת״ ('this') is a limiting word. It leaves out the חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One excluded by writing 'this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the same פסוק also has a limiting word, ״זֹאת״, and that word takes the bird out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the פסוק has two forces. ״תּוֹרַת״ includes, and ״זֹאת״ excludes. The result is that the inner חטאות are in and the bird is out, which matches the ברייתא from step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Excluded; a word that narrows the law
'This,' a limiting word in the פסוק

phrases.english: The Merciful One excluded by writing 'this.'

steps.confusionAlert: ״תּוֹרַת״ and ״זֹאת״ come from the same short phrase (זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַחַטָּאת). One word adds, and the other takes away. The next step asks how we know which חטאת each word applies to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in the פסוק

steps.title: Why include the inner offerings and not the bird?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we use ״תּוֹרַת״ to include the inner חטאות and ״זֹאת״ to exclude the bird. Maybe it should be the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to decide this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the two words were assigned. Why does the including word go to the inner חטאות, and the excluding word go to the bird?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings could fit the words. We could have said ״תּוֹרַת״ includes the bird and ״זֹאת״ excludes the inner חטאות. The גמרא wants a reason for the choice that was made.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And what did you see?' Why did you choose this way and not the opposite?

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He means: what made you decide to include the inner ones and leave out the bird, and not the opposite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the words of steps 12 and 14 were assigned
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying ״תּוֹרַת״ to the inner חטאות and ״זֹאת״ to the bird
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opposite assignment is just as possible from the wording, so a reason is needed

steps.title: Inner animal sin offerings are more similar to eaten ones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer. It makes sense to include the inner animal חטאות, because they share many features with the eaten חטאות: they are animals, they are slaughtered in the north, and their blood is collected in a vessel. The list continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the inner animal sin offerings should be the ones included, since they are animals, they are slaughtered in the north, and their blood is collected in a vessel,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer. It lists ways the inner חטאות are like the eaten חטאות, and the list keeps going after this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a פסוק includes one thing and excludes another, we include whatever is more similar to the main case. Inner חטאות share many features with eaten חטאות. A bird shares far fewer of them. So the inner ones go in, and the bird stays out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense,' a reasoning-based answer
To include
Slaughter on the north side of the עזרה
Catching the blood in a holy vessel

phrases.english: It makes sense that inner animal sin offerings
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method of the גמרא. When one word includes and another excludes, we include whatever is closer to the main case.
